- When sentiment is predominantly positive (≥ 1.0) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion bias.
- When sentiment turns negative (≤ -1.0) or shows strong reversal signals, model often underestimates; adjust upward to reflect sentiment-driven rebound potential.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior period), model frequently overshoots in subsequent days; apply a downward correction of 2–5% to avoid overreaction.
- In periods of high volatility or erratic sentiment shifts, model exhibits lag in responding to new sentiment; delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days if sentiment changes abruptly.
- If model consistently forecasts higher than true outcome in early days of a 30-day window, it may be overconfident; apply a 1–3% downward bias to early forecast points.
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative sentiment followed by positive, model often fails to capture the “bounce” — increase forecast sensitivity to sentiment reversal signals in the 3–5 day window after sentiment flip.
